simple.meaning: תְּדִירָא (tᵉdîyrâʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “permanence , i.e. (adverb) constantly.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 6:17. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּדִירָא (H8411) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תְּדִירָא (tᵉdîyrâʼ) / H8411 is traced through Daniel 6:17, Daniel 6:21 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8411. tedira תְּדִירָא noun feminine continuance ( ᵑ7 id. ; see Biblical Hebrew דּוּר ); — absolute in phrase ׳בִּת continually Dan 6:17 ; 6:21 .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) from 1753 in the original sense of enduring;

occurrences.englishText: A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!
